detail.body:
## Motivation

The coarse histogram bin comes from the top bits of the fp16 cast, so one bin spans a quarter-binade. The collect pass stores at most 2048 threshold-bin candidates; when the bin is larger, `handle_tie` ranks whichever arrived first and silently returns a wrong top-k set.

Found while profiling GLM-5.2 decode on MI355X: ~0.04% of rows entered this path across all 8 ranks, with a largest observed bin of 4139 against the 2048 cap and none of those rows bit-identical. #35257 reports the same defect independently from the CUDA side — referenced, not closed.

## Modifications

When the threshold bin overflows, narrow it with three exact-key radix rounds (12 / 12 / 8 bits), then make one final input scan to emit candidates above the selected bucket and re-stage the bucket for the existing tie handler. The refinement histogram overlays the dead arrival-order buffer, so LDS is unchanged.

The cold scan uses a separate reversed-lane load path. This keeps its load-address state out of the fast path's registers and restores most of the CUDA regression reported in review.

Replace the fp16-bin boundary conversion with exact fp32 bounds. In particular, when a bin's high edge is `+0.0`, the boundary advances to the smallest positive subnormal so `-0.0` cannot be misclassified as above the bin.

The ROCm long-row split path from #39931 gets the same refinement: each block publishes its uncapped bin count, and the last block refines the whole row when the bin overflows.

The fast path only adds the overflow comparison. The ROCm `__launch_bounds__` argument also states the physical floor of 4 waves/SIMD; the CUDA spelling is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

The exactness test covers register, streaming and split (4×65536) shapes with six distributions, including adjacent fp32 values and `-0.0`; on CUDA it skips rows longer than 24576, which can reach the still-unrefined cluster path.

| suite | result before the fix |
|---|---|
| 300 pre-existing cases | 300 passed |
| 10 overflowing non-identical cases | 10 failed |
| 2 `all_equal` controls | 2 passed |

The signed-zero cases also fail on the pre-review refinement and pass with the new boundary conversion. All 330 cases pass on the merged tree; on the split shape, 4 of the 6 distributions failed before the refinement.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

MI355X (gfx950), five paired runs per arm on one GPU, 200 iterations after warmup:

| distribution | shape | main | this PR | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `randn` (hot path) | 6×8192 | 5.430 µs | 5.338 µs | −1.7% |
| `randn` (hot path) | 4×32768 | 12.270 µs | 12.188 µs | −0.7% |
| `narrow_bin` | 6×8192 | 16.821 µs | 20.937 µs | +24.5% |
| `narrow_bin` | 4×32768 | 29.652 µs | 50.030 µs | +68.7% |
| `two_values` (32-bit refinement) | 6×8192 | 11.487 µs | 34.862 µs | +203.5% |
| `two_values` (32-bit refinement) | 4×32768 | 36.314 µs | 117.756 µs | +224.3% |

The cold-path delta is the cost of exact work that main skips by returning a wrong answer. It is entered on ~0.04% of rows in the serving traffic above. Against the previous PR implementation, the new scan is 2.6–5.3% faster on `narrow_bin`. On the latest tree, a clean local JIT build is 10.50 s versus 10.02 s on main (+4.8%), rather than the nearly 2× CUDA increase reported before this rewrite.

Without overflow the split path is unchanged (15.5–20.1 µs for batch 1–8, 64K–128K, before and after).

On gfx950: 63 → 71 VGPRs, zero spills, LDS unchanged at 26928 B. We do not have NVIDIA hardware; CUDA register pressure and B200 performance need CI/reviewer measurement.

## Known gap

The CUDA-only `TopKCluster` path still truncates. Refining there needs cluster-wide histogram and emit counters rather than the block-local ones used here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add exactness tests.
- [x] Provide accuracy and performance results.
- [x] Keep documentation and comments synchronized.

+# --- exactness when the coarse histogram cannot discriminate -----------------
+# The tests above draw from ``torch.randn``, which spreads scores over many
+# coarse bins and leaves the threshold bin far below the tie-staging capacity.
+# These distributions force the threshold bin to overflow the staging buffer.
+NARROW_DISTRIBUTIONS = [
+    "narrow",
+    "narrow_bin",
+    "tiny",
+    "two_values",
+    "signed_zero",
+    "all_equal",
+]
+
+
+def _single_bin_scores(kind, batch, width, device):
+    """Scores whose coarse bin carries no ordering information.
+
+    The bin comes from the top bits of the fp16 cast, so a band narrower than
+    one fp16 ulp -- or a magnitude that underflows fp16 -- gives one bin.
+    """
+    if kind == "narrow":
+        # Narrower than one fp32 ulp at 1.0 (1.19e-7): pins the tie count.
+        u = torch.rand(batch, width, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) * 2.0 - 1.0
+        return 1.0 + u * 1e-6
+    if kind == "narrow_bin":
+        # One coarse bin, ~1.7e5 distinct fp32 values: pins the ordering too.
+        return 1.0 + torch.rand(batch, width, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) * 0.02
+    if kind == "tiny":
+        # Below the fp16 subnormal floor: every score casts to zero.
+        return (
+            0.5 + torch.rand(batch, width, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+        ) * 1e-30
+    if kind == "two_values":
+        # Two adjacent fp32 values, ~half the row each: the refinement has to
+        # consume all 32 bits before the survivors are bit-identical, and more
+        # than kMaxNumTie of them still remain at that point.
+        hi = torch.tensor(1.0, dtype=torch.float32, device=device).nextafter(
+            torch.tensor(2.0, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+        )
+        pick = torch.rand(batch, width, device=device) < 0.5
+        return torch.where(pick, hi, torch.ones_like(hi))
+    if kind == "signed_zero":
+        # The threshold bin ends at +0.0. Its upper boundary must move to the
+        # smallest positive subnormal so -0.0 stays in the tie set instead of
+        # racing true positive values for output slots.
+        out = torch.full((batch, width), -1.0, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+        out[:, : width // 2] = -0.0
+        out[:, -1024:] = 1e-6
+        return out
+    # Control: the bin overflows too, but the candidates are bit-identical, so
+    # any subset is correct and this must keep passing.
+    return torch.full((batch, width), 0.5, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+
+
+def _narrow_seed(dist, *rest):
+    """Reproducible across processes -- ``hash(str)`` is salted per interpreter."""
+    seed = NARROW_DISTRIBUTIONS.index(dist)
+    for v in rest:
+        seed = seed * 100003 + int(v)
+    return seed
+
+
+# Longest row that never reaches the CUDA cluster path, which still truncates an
+# overflowing threshold bin (the smallest get_static_cluster_floor in topk_v2.cuh).
+CUDA_MAX_NON_CLUSTER_SEQ = 24576
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dist", NARROW_DISTRIBUTIONS)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("batch,seq", [(6, 8192), (4, 20480), (4, 32768), (4, 65536)])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_topk_v2_single_coarse_bin_is_exact(batch: int, seq: int, dist: str) -> None:
+    """No tolerance here: the threshold bin holds the whole row at k=2048, so a
+    dropped candidate is a wrong answer rather than a tie swap. Covers
+    register-path and streaming-path shapes, and a ROCm split-path shape (above
+    split_floor); tie staging is per-template.
+    """
+    if not is_hip() and seq > CUDA_MAX_NON_CLUSTER_SEQ:
+        pytest.skip("CUDA may route this shape to the unrefined cluster path")
+    torch.manual_seed(_narrow_seed(dist, batch, seq))
+    device = "cuda"
+    k = 2048
+    width = (seq + 3) & ~3
+    scores = _single_bin_scores(dist, batch, width, device)[:, :seq]
+    seq_lens = torch.full((batch,), seq, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+
+    our_raw = _run_raw(scores, seq_lens, k)
+    ref_raw = _reference(scores, seq_lens, k)
+    _assert_topk_close(
+        scores.cpu(), ref_raw, our_raw, batch, seq_lens.cpu(), k, max_permit_error=0
+    )
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dist", ["narrow_bin", "two_values"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("length", [8192, 40000])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_topk_v2_ragged_single_coarse_bin(dist: str, length: int) -> None:
+    """Overflow refinement on an unaligned ragged window.
+
+    The refinement re-reads candidates through ``for_each_input`` and has to
+    agree with the collect pass on which elements exist. A window whose start is
+    not 4-aligned makes the kernel mask the columns it pulls in ahead of the
+    window, so this pins that the masked head stays out of both counts. Runs a
+    register-path and a streaming-path length with no tie tolerance.
+    """
+    k = 2048
+    torch.manual_seed(_narrow_seed(dist, length, 2))
+    device = "cuda"
+    starts = [0, 1, 2, 3, 5]
+    rows = len(starts)
+    width = (max(starts) + length + 3) & ~3
+    scores = torch.full(
+        (rows, width), OUTSIDE_SCORE, dtype=torch.float32, device=device
+    )
+    band = _single_bin_scores(dist, rows, length, device)
+    for i, s in enumerate(starts):
+        scores[i, s : s + length] = band[i]
+    before = scores.clone()
+    starts_t = torch.tensor(starts, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    lengths = torch.full((rows,), length, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+
+    our_raw = _run_ragged(scores, lengths, starts_t, starts_t + 4321, k)
+
+    windows = torch.empty(rows, length, dtype=torch.float32)
+    for i, s in enumerate(starts):
+        windows[i] = before[i, s : s + length].cpu()
+    ref_raw = _reference(windows, lengths.cpu(), k)
+    _assert_topk_close(
+        windows, ref_raw, our_raw, rows, lengths.cpu(), k, max_permit_error=0
+    )
+

+        # Below the fp16 subnormal floor: every score casts to zero.
+        return (
+            0.5 + torch.rand(batch, width, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+        ) * 1e-30
+    if kind == "two_values":
+        # Two adjacent fp32 values, ~half the row each: the refinement has to
+        # consume all 32 bits before the survivors are bit-identical, and more
+        # than kMaxNumTie of them still remain at that point.
+        hi = torch.tensor(1.0, dtype=torch.float32, device=device).nextafter(
+            torch.tensor(2.0, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+        )
+        pick = torch.rand(batch, width, device=device) < 0.5
+        return torch.where(pick, hi, torch.ones_like(hi))
+    if kind == "signed_zero":
+        # The threshold bin ends at +0.0. Its upper boundary must move to the
+        # smallest positive subnormal so -0.0 stays in the tie set instead of
+        # racing true positive values for output slots.
+        out = torch.full((batch, width), -1.0, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+        out[:, : width // 2] = -0.0
+        out[:, -1024:] = 1e-6
+        return out
+    # Control: the bin overflows too, but the candidates are bit-identical, so
+    # any subset is correct and this must keep passing.
+    return torch.full((batch, width), 0.5, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+
+
+def _narrow_seed(dist, *rest):
+    """Reproducible across processes -- ``hash(str)`` is salted per interpreter."""
+    seed = NARROW_DISTRIBUTIONS.index(dist)
+    for v in rest:
+        seed = seed * 100003 + int(v)
+    return seed
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not is_hip(), reason="CUDA may route these shapes to the unrefined cluster path"

inline_comments.body: Why do we introduce overhead in the fast-path and add to the complexity? Please explain why the original implementation cannot work. In this PR we deliberately skip cluster's case since it's another problem. For the HIP path, all of them are already correct. We should be aware that, as long as `# >= v_hi` is no larger than topk, while `# >= v_lo` is no less than topk, the algorithm is 100% correct. Relaxing `v_hi` from 0.0 to subnormal positive number is not a correctness issue.

You are right: with the subnormal `v_hi` the refined paths stay exact, and the case only breaks the cluster path, which this PR leaves out. Reverted in 9bb88de911; CUDA still runs the narrow shapes that cannot reach the cluster path.

On the reported H200 regression (batch-31 persistent case ~1% slower, cold build ~14% longer): compiling topk_v2 for sm_90a locally, registers and spills match main, but the force-inlined `refine_ties` copies add ~19% SASS overall and ~26% to `topk_main_kernel<true, 3, *>`, so I think code size is the cause. This was already in the version you approved. Two options:
1. Build the refinement for ROCm only, so CUDA compiles to the same code as main.
2. Make `refine_ties` `__noinline__` to keep CUDA exact. I can only check this statically (no NVIDIA GPU here), so it would need an H200 re-run.

Which do you prefer, and should it go into this PR or a follow-up?
Per DarkSharpness's review, reverted in 9bb88de911: the register, streaming and split paths stay exact with the subnormal `v_hi`, and the cluster path's overflow handling is out of scope for this PR.

Local check of the build time: a cold sm_90a compile of the topk_v2 module (CUDA 13.0, same flags as the JIT, ninja -j1, 3 interleaved runs) takes 11.10 s on main and 12.64 s on this PR, +14%, which matches the reported number.

Per DarkSharpness, keeping `refine_ties` as approved, without `__noinline__`: he measured only a very small CUDA overhead on that version, and `__noinline__` does not guarantee better performance. With the -0.0 change reverted, the CUDA code here matches the approved version; the remaining diff is the test running the narrow shapes on CUDA that cannot reach the cluster path.

@DarkSharpness thanks — all three addressed in c05fe161c9, and measured on MI355X.

**The min/max early-out is gone.** You are right that it was paying a scan on every refinement to serve a degenerate case. Without it the radix rounds still terminate correctly on an all-equal row: they consume all 32 bits and then truncate a bit-identical set, which is exact. Removing it also freed the tie staging buffer, which this path does not need — it re-derives the candidates rather than trusting what the collect pass staged there — so the buffer now carries the histogram.

**Down to at most four passes.** Two changes got there. The radix is 12 bits instead of 8, using that freed buffer (it is exactly `kRefineSize` uint32 wide, so the shared-memory footprint is unchanged at 27392 B), which covers the 32-bit key in three rounds instead of four. And each round's emit is fused with the next round's histogram: one scan classifies a candidate as above / equal / below the round's threshold digit and does both. So the cost is one pass to seed the first histogram plus one per round — four worst case, two if the bin resolves in the first round.

**The staging pass is eliminated too**, fused into the last round's emit the same way.

Kernel time, 200 iterations after warmup:

| distribution | shape | before | after | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `randn` (no overflow, hot path) | 6×8192 | 5.604 µs | 5.596 µs | −0.1% |
| `randn` (no overflow, hot path) | 4×32768 | 12.507 µs | 12.475 µs | −0.3% |
| `narrow_bin` (every row refines) | 6×8192 | 34.825 µs | 22.482 µs | −35.4% |
| `narrow_bin` (every row refines) | 4×32768 | 75.559 µs | 53.223 µs | −29.6% |
| `two_values` (worst case, 32 bits) | 6×8192 | 53.509 µs | 36.354 µs | −32.1% |
| `two_values` (worst case, 32 bits) | 4×32768 | 168.130 µs | 119.571 µs | −28.9% |

The hot path is unchanged, as it should be — it still only pays the `equal_count > kMaxNumTie` comparison.

On correctness after the rewrite: the suite is 288/288 on this branch. Run against the unfixed kernel on main it is 8 failed / 2 passed, the two passes being the `all_equal` controls, so the tests still discriminate. `two_values` is new and covers the exit the early-out used to stand in front of: two adjacent fp32 values at roughly half the row each, so the refinement has to consume all 32 bits and still has more than `kMaxNumTie` survivors at that point. Register usage is 78 VGPRs with zero spills, up from 57 on main.

@DarkSharpness when you have a moment — the performance changes you asked for are in `fcd39053bd`, and CI is now green on the jobs that cover this kernel.

The branch has also been rebased onto latest `main`. That job runs three test files and none of them is a top-k test, so this kernel never executes in it.

Happy to dig into any of those if you would rather they were green first.

Hi. Could you please temporarily hold on until https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38798 is merged? Sorry we're actively working on that and it should land within next few days. I will check this PR in detail later. This topk kernel is very sensitive in register usage on CUDA, and any seemingly irrelevant test might lead to wild performance data, so I will take a very detailed look at this PR later. Please stay tuned. Thanks :)

Sounds good, we'll hold.

Two things worth flagging while we wait.

The truncation this PR fixes is unchanged in #38798 — the `if (pos < kMaxNumTie)` drop in the collect pass and the `min(count_eq, kMaxNumTie)` clip are both still there, on the register, streaming and cluster paths. So the kernel will still return a wrong top-k set when a threshold coarse bin overflows.

And please don't try to carry this change into #38798; it is safer for us to re-port it afterwards. The refinement re-reads candidates from global memory and relies on `for_each_input` visiting exactly the elements the collect pass counted. #38798 pads the last vector with `padding_value()` and compensates with `atomicSub` on the histogram, which breaks that invariant — easy to miss in a mechanical merge, and the failure mode would be a silently wrong refinement.

On your register point: we only have MI355X here, so every number in this PR is gfx950 (57 to 78 VGPRs, no spills, LDS unchanged). We cannot measure the CUDA side at all. If that is the main concern, it would help if someone with an NVIDIA box could check it — or tell us which shapes and metric you want and we will get them into the PR another way.

Ping me when #38798 lands and I'll rebase, re-measure and re-request review.

Rebased onto #39648 and re-ported, now `e503afa6bd`.

A correction to what I said earlier: I claimed the padding change would break the refinement's counting invariant. That was wrong. `padding_value()` is `quiet_NaN()`, and NaN fails both `val >= v_hi` and `val >= v_lo`, so padding is counted by neither `count_gt` nor `count_eq` — the ragged path even writes the NaN into the score buffer itself. Since `for_each_input` visits exactly `[0, seq_len)`, the collect pass and the refinement's re-read agree on which elements exist, and no extra handling was needed. There is now a test that pins this rather than leaving it to code reading: overflow on an unaligned ragged window, which fails on the kernel on main.

Also worth flagging: #39648 restructured the kernel but left all four truncation sites unchanged, so the defect is exactly as it was.
